title: Which harness do you use for your coding?
author: SimCFB
selftext:
When I say harness I mean something like. This is what I typically use

1) VsCode + Codex extension

2) VsCode + Claude Code extension

3) VsCode + Kilo code extension specifically to use Grok Code in vscode (because it doesn't or at least didn't when I look have an a native extension)

4) ChatGPT native app. Lately been using that more for codex. I've been told it's very good with Astra.

What is your setup?

I read that the harness can make a big difference in how good your coding results are and how many tokens it wastes. But I've only ever really worked with those 4.

I tried cursor at first but didn't stick with it.

comments.author: EC36339
comments.body:
VSCode is abysmally terrible for agentic coding.

It's a text editor trying to be too many things. And it's a terrible text editor, too.

I use Claude Code, because I can use it from my phone. That way I can work on my game from anywhere. It's so much better to not have to sit in front a computer for tasks that don't require a computer, but only a brain, a prompt, and a Linux container (that is faster than Github actions containers btw. Twice as fast. What Amish village is Microsoft hosting their shit in?!)

I can solve problems in my head while I'm out hiking, then communicate with the AI whenever I came up with a solution. Or the other way round. It doesn't matter if the AI is slow, or if a problem or decision is difficult and I am slow, because I'm not sitting in a dark room in front of a screen and feeling the pressure to make the most of my time while my body is in an unhealthy position. Being outside means having infinite patience, because not a single moment is wasted.

Sometimes I also use OpenCode with DeepSeek V4 Flash via DeepSeek API. DS is much faster and communicates more clearly, and it is still cheap af. But I can't use it remotely. There's probably a way to make that possible with a custom setup, but I haven't had time to experiment with that, yet, and OpenCode has known security issues and a track record of bad practices, so I'd rather not have it open listening sockets anywhere.
